newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Norilsk nickel output to rise 20 pct in 1997 yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Norilsk nickel output to rise 20 pct in 1997 yr/yr.

text.p: Russia's RAO Norilsk Nikel aims to produce 213,000 tonnes of nickel in 1997, up 20 percent from 177,185 tonnes in 1996, Sergei Vetchinin, group spokesman, said on Monday.
He also said copper output would rise nine percent this year to 370,000 tonnes from 340,000 last year, and cobalt output by 30 percent to 4,100 tonnes from 3,151 tonnes in 1995.

"According to our plan for the years 1996 to 2000, the Norilsk Nickel group proposes by the end of this year to hit the following targets -- 213,000 tonnes of nickel, 370,000 tonnes of copper and 4,100 tonnes of cobalt," Vetchinin told Reuters.
He was clarifying a statement by the group in February which gave the same output targets but said they would be reached by the end of 2000.

"We think these output targets are realistic," he said. He said the group was increasing efficiency at its production units and transferring major social costs on to municipal budgets. He noted that the group had already boosted nickel output by nine percent year-on-year during the first five months of 1997.

Analysts have said that freeing up more cash to reinvest in the company's huge mining and processing facilities was crucial to its long-term survival. Norilsk ran up huge financial losses last year, partly because of the massive social burden it carries in supporting the Arctic town of Norilsk.
